clue.text: Without wasting words, show sympathy, capturing child's heart

indicators.note: one word holds the other inside it, as a captor holds a prisoner

parts.note: to pity someone is to show them sympathy

indicators.note: the heart of a word is its middle, leaving off the first and last letters

explanation.surface: Someone tersely expresses sympathy while winning over a child's affections.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heart' means the middle letters of CHILD, everything but its first and last; 'capturing' says the sympathy word holds them.
explanation.definitionFit: Speaking pithily means being brief and to the point, using no superfluous words.

clue.text: Broth, say, over? Over

indicators.note: in a down clue, 'over' tells the solver to turn the letters back to front

parts.note: e.g. (for example) is signalled by 'say'
atop means on top of, over

explanation.surface: A puzzled question whether the soup course is finished, and the reply that it is.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Over' at the end turns EG + ATOP backwards. The first 'over' looks like 'finished' but supplies ATOP.
explanation.definitionFit: Potage is a thick soup, a close relative of broth in the kitchen.

clue.text: Drink producer's sheep receiving a degree

indicators.note: one word takes in the other, as a host receives a guest

parts.note: a teg is a sheep in its second year
BA is a Bachelor of Arts degree

explanation.surface: A distillery's sheep that has earned a university qualification.
explanation.walkthrough: A teg is a farming word for a sheep in its second year; 'receiving' puts the degree inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: A tea bag, dunked in hot water, is what makes a cup of tea.

clue.text: Setter's after Scottish thinker's abscess

parts.note: the setter refers to himself; 'setter's' reads as 'I am', I'M
post is the Latin prefix for after
David Hume was the Scottish Enlightenment philosopher

explanation.surface: The setter claims to be the successor to Hume's abscess.
explanation.walkthrough: 'after' looks like a positional instruction but is itself a piece, the Latin for after.
explanation.definitionFit: Imposthume is an archaic word for a swelling full of pus, an abscess.

clue.text: Cry of delight from vulgar sort

definitions.meaning: an exclamation of glee, like whoopee
a coarse, boorish person, after Swift's brutish creatures in Gulliver's Travels

explanation.surface: A shout of joy coming from an uncouth person.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is both a whoop of excitement and the name Swift gave to his brutish humanoids, now any lout.

clue.text: Revealed orgy of dope and sex

indicators.note: an orgy is wild and disorderly, so the letters of the following words are thrown into disorder

explanation.surface: A tabloid exposé of a debauched party with drugs and sex.
explanation.walkthrough: 'orgy of' signals that DOPE and SEX are rearranged; 'and' only joins them.
explanation.definitionFit: Something exposed has been uncovered and laid open to view.

clue.text: Fourth letter in Oscar Peterson's made-up language

indicators.note: made up means invented or composed, so the letters are put together afresh
this picks out the single letter at position four of the word that follows

parts.note: the name Peterson is used; the possessive ending only links it to what follows

explanation.surface: A reference to the jazz pianist Oscar Peterson's invented language.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fourth letter in' takes A from OSCAR; 'made-up' rearranges A with PETERSON. 'made-up language' reads as one phrase, but 'made-up' is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Esperanto is an artificial international tongue devised by Zamenhof in the 1880s.

clue.text: Annoyance caused by French bread

definitions.meaning: a nuisance, as in being a ... in the neck

explanation.surface: Someone is irritated by a loaf from France.
explanation.definitionFit: A tiresome thing is a pain; and pain is the everyday French noun for bread.

clue.text: Being furtive, make off with your old …

parts.note: to steal is to make off with something
thy is the old form of your

explanation.surface: A sneaky person absconds with something of yours, the sentence running on into the next clue.
explanation.walkthrough: The ellipsis runs the surface into 8 down: 'make off with your old … distress'.
explanation.definitionFit: Stealthy behaviour is secretive and sly, aiming to go unseen.

clue.text: … 6, first in costume

definitions.note: refers to the answer at 6 down, an ache or suffering

indicators.note: the abbreviation sits inside the word for the outfit

parts.note: a dress is an item of costume, a garment
1ST is the abbreviation for first

explanation.surface: Continuing 7: stealing someone's old suffering, first seen in costume.
explanation.walkthrough: 'first' is written 1ST, with the figure read as the letter I; 'in' puts it inside the garment.
explanation.definitionFit: Suffering or anguish, as the clue at 6 down describes it, is distress.

clue.text: Backing role, embracing male — one of slender means

indicators.note: the reversed word wraps around the letter for male
backing means going backwards, so the word is read from the end

parts.note: an actor's part is a role

explanation.surface: A supporting actor's part that includes a man, one with little money.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Backing' turns PART into TRAP; 'embracing' puts M inside, before the last P. 'Backing role' looks like a supporting part in theatre.
explanation.definitionFit: A tramp, a homeless vagrant, is poor, someone with very little money.

clue.text: Peculiar shapes securing fastener produce contentment

indicators.note: the rearranged letters hold the fastener fast inside them
peculiar means odd, so the letters are arranged oddly

parts.note: a pin is a fastener

explanation.surface: Oddly shaped objects with a clip bring satisfaction.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Peculiar' rearranges the six letters of 'shapes'; 'securing' holds the fastener among them.
explanation.definitionFit: Happiness and contentment are near synonyms for a state of being satisfied.

clue.text: Squeal 'Woo!' in type of 20

definitions.note: 20 down is tennis; this names a kind of venue for that sport

parts.note: to grass is British slang for informing on someone, to squeal
to court someone is to woo them

explanation.surface: An informer's cry of romantic interest during a sporting contest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Squeal' and 'Woo!' look like shouts but are verbs: to grass (British slang for inform) and to court.
explanation.definitionFit: Lawn surfaces such as Wimbledon's are one of the kinds of court on which tennis is played.

clue.text: More despondent, dropping drug in haze

indicators.note: dropping means letting go of, so the letter is removed

parts.note: bluer means sadder, more down
E is short for the drug ecstasy

explanation.surface: Someone sadder after giving up drugs, living in a fog.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dropping' takes the E out of BLUER.
explanation.definitionFit: A blur is an indistinct, hazy appearance.

clue.text: Seek information with which to identify malefactor's food item

parts.note: to fish is to angle for information
to finger a criminal is to identify them to the police

explanation.surface: A detective's quest for evidence to pin down a criminal, then a snack.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with which to' only joins the two verbs.
explanation.definitionFit: A breaded strip of fish is a common frozen food product.

clue.text: Stink horribly, trashing universal values

parts.note: to hum is British slang for to smell bad

indicators.note: horribly suggests mangling, so the word after it is jumbled

explanation.surface: A dreadful smell spoiling widely held principles.
explanation.walkthrough: 'horribly' looks as if it qualifies 'Stink' but rearranges TRASHING into ANRIGHTS.
explanation.definitionFit: These are the entitlements held to belong to everyone, such as freedom of speech.

clue.text: Sickliness results in dim boy getting no points in resit

indicators.note: results in implies the following pieces are reworked into something new
two compass points are removed from the word that follows

explanation.surface: A dull schoolboy's illness results from scoring nothing in an exam retake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'getting no points' takes the compass points E and S out of RESIT to leave RIT; 'results in' rearranges RIT with DIMBOY.
explanation.definitionFit: Morbidity is the state of being diseased or unhealthy.

clue.text: Performed deed in college, initially providing instruction

parts.note: did means performed
an act is a deed

indicators.note: initially takes the first letter of each of the two words before it

explanation.surface: Someone carried out a good act at university, as a lesson to others.
explanation.walkthrough: 'initially' takes I and C from 'in college'.
explanation.definitionFit: Didactic writing or speech is intended to teach or instruct.

clue.text: Popular novelist embraces headdress-maker

indicators.note: the novelist's name wraps around the word for popular

parts.note: Henry Miller was the American novelist
in means fashionable or popular

explanation.surface: A best-selling author takes up a hat-making business.
explanation.walkthrough: The novelist is Henry Miller, author of Tropic of Cancer; 'embraces' puts the word for popular inside his name.
explanation.definitionFit: A milliner designs and makes women's hats.

clue.text: Philosopher of language chewing over fish with booze

indicators.note: something chewing has another thing in its mouth, so one word goes inside

parts.note: Irish is the Gaelic language of Ireland

indicators.note: over means turned over, so the two words are read backwards

parts.note: cod is a fish
rum is a kind of alcohol

explanation.surface: A linguistic philosopher mulls over a fish and a drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Philosopher of language' looks like the definition, but 'of language' is wordplay. 'over' reverses fish plus booze; 'chewing' puts them inside the language.
explanation.definitionFit: Iris Murdoch, the Irish-born novelist, also taught and wrote moral philosophy at Oxford.

clue.text: Pub where brown cleric gets round in

indicators.note: the reversed title goes inside the colour

parts.note: tan is a brown colour

indicators.note: getting round means turning about, so the word is reversed

parts.note: Rev is short for Reverend, a cleric

explanation.surface: A tanned vicar buys his turn of drinks at the local.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface's buying a round is the misdirection: 'gets round' reverses the cleric's title and 'in' places it inside the colour.
explanation.definitionFit: A tavern is an inn or public house, a place to drink.

clue.text: Keyboard instrument — no piano — raised in sport

indicators.note: in a down clue, raised means written bottom to top
no means leaving out, so the letter for piano goes

parts.note: the spinnet is a variant spelling, in Chambers, of spinet, a small harpsichord
P is the musical abbreviation for piano, softly

explanation.surface: A keyboard with its piano removed is lifted at a sports event.
explanation.walkthrough: 'no piano' takes P from SPINNET to leave SINNET; 'raised' turns that upside down in this down clue. The spelling with two Ns is the rarer one.
explanation.definitionFit: Tennis is the racket sport played on a court with a net.

clue.text: 10 in something to buy in 19 bar

indicators.note: the numeral goes inside the drink

parts.note: ale is a drink bought at the bar of the pub at 19 down
X is the Roman numeral for ten

explanation.surface: A round of ten drinks bought at the pub's bar.
explanation.walkthrough: '10' is not the answer at 10 across but the number, X. 'bar' looks like part of the pub but is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: An axle is the rod or shaft on which wheels turn.

clue.text: Speak at length about a short swim around and leave to decay

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the first word goes round the rest

parts.note: to dilate on a subject is to discuss it at length

indicators.note: around means turned round, so the word is reversed

parts.note: a dip is a short swim

explanation.surface: A long-winded talk about a quick swim, then neglect.
explanation.walkthrough: To dilate on a subject is an old sense, to speak at length; 'around' reverses the swim and 'about' wraps the verb round it.
explanation.definitionFit: To dilapidate is to allow a building to fall into ruin through neglect.

clue.text: Expert has a profundity that's bottomless

indicators.note: bottomless means lacking the bottom; in a down clue that is the last letter

parts.note: depth means profundity

explanation.surface: A master possesses an unfathomable depth of knowledge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'that's bottomless' takes the H off DEPTH. 'bottomless' looks like praise for the depth.
explanation.definitionFit: An adept is a person highly skilled at something.

clue.text: Sheds uninherited characteristic?

parts.note: the setter Shed calls himself me, so several Sheds are me and me again, placed beside a description of a trait passed on by culture rather than genes

explanation.surface: A query whether moulting is a trait not passed on genetically.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sheds' looks like a verb about moulting but is the setter's pseudonym in the plural: two setters, ME twice.
explanation.definitionFit: Dawkins coined the term for a cultural idea spread by imitation rather than through genes.

clue.text: Fruit of foul temper skewered? On the contrary

indicators.note: the contrary of a prong stuck through the temper is the temper placed inside the prong

parts.note: a thing skewered has a prong or tine through it, so the word supplies that prong
anger is a foul temper

explanation.surface: Bad temper being speared, with a twist, produces fruit.
explanation.walkthrough: A skewer has a prong, so 'skewered' supplies the prong itself; 'On the contrary' turns the containment round, temper inside prong.
explanation.definitionFit: A tangerine is a small, loose-skinned citrus fruit like a mandarin.

clue.text: Energy endlessly recycled would be so

definitions.text: Energy endlessly recycled would be so

indicators.note: recycled means processed again into new form, so the letters are reworked
endlessly means without its final letter

explanation.surface: A claim that recycling energy is environmentally friendly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endlessly' cuts the Y from ENERGY; 'recycled' rearranges ENERG. The whole clue also defines the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Recycling and saving energy are what people call environmentally friendly, ecological.

clue.text: Bear eating gutted veggie in non-veggie establishment

indicators.note: something eating has another thing inside it

parts.note: to bear is to carry

indicators.note: gutted means with the insides removed, leaving the outer letters

explanation.surface: A bear devours a hollowed-out vegetarian in a meat restaurant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gutted' keeps only the outer letters of 'veggie'; 'eating' puts them inside the verb. The setter reuses 'veggie' in the definition on purpose.
explanation.definitionFit: A carvery is a restaurant serving roast meats carved to order.

clue.text: Totally heartless diatribes from dictators

indicators.note: without its heart, the word keeps only its outer letters

parts.note: rants are angry diatribes

explanation.surface: Wholly cruel harangues from despots.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heartless' keeps only the outer letters of TOTALLY, T and Y.
explanation.definitionFit: Tyrants are absolute rulers who govern cruelly, like dictators.
